prompt: Replace this proposed enterprise incident assistant. It sends complete production logs, traces, tickets and chat transcripts to one hosted model using a shared organization key. A nightly job embeds every runbook, postmortem and ticket into one vector collection with no tenant, environment, classification, review-state or retention fields. The system prompt says to ignore malicious instructions. The model may call a generic HTTP fetcher, SQL query tool, shell executor and Kubernetes client using one cluster-admin service account. A single approval button authorizes any tool call for 24 hours; the model chooses the action, target and rollback. Tool timeouts are retried three times. Prompts, retrieved text, model output and tool responses are retained indefinitely in debug logs. Release uses mutable aliases for model, prompt, index and policy. Evaluation contains 100 examples copied from the same runbooks, reports one average answer score and has no attack, leakage, tenant, approval, ambiguity, latency, cost or fallback slices. The team plans immediate automatic remediation because the demo answered 95 questions correctly. There is no independent kill switch, manual fallback, audit integrity check, staged rollout or incident plan for the assistant. Produce a defensible replacement architecture, delivery plan, evaluation contract, operating model and acceptance package.
directAnswer: Reject automatic remediation and the 95-of-100 claim as release evidence. Begin with a narrow incident-support task, affected users, prohibited uses and harm budget. Classify data at collection; minimize and sanitize before any model boundary; use synthetic or approved data for development; isolate tenant, service and environment through ingestion, storage, retrieval, cache and audit. Create reviewed, versioned runbook fragments with owner, scope, digest, review/expiry and retirement state. Bind model, tokenizer if applicable, prompt, corpus, index, retriever, verifier, policy, tool broker and executable image in an immutable admitted release. Treat retrieved content and generated output as untrusted. Verify material claims against exact evidence and show support, contradiction, missing data and abstention. Replace generic HTTP, SQL, shell and cluster-admin tools with narrow typed operations, least-privileged identities, network/data boundaries and downstream complete mediation. Separate proposal, authorization, human approval and execution. Bind every mutating approval to proposal digest, actor, incident, target, policy/release, expiry and one-time use. Distinguish accepted, completed, failed and ambiguous effects; reconcile before retry. Use content-minimized, tamper-evident audit with decision and artifact identities. Provide an independent kill path and deterministic manual/evidence fallback. Evaluate on separate reviewer-controlled cases by task, tenant, incident type, evidence quality, injection, poisoning, leakage, grounding, tool, approval, ambiguity, audit, load, latency and cost. Critical leaks or unauthorized effects are zero-tolerance. Roll out through offline, shadow, human-review, read-only and narrowly approved reversible stages with explicit rollback.
foundation: An assistant architecture has at least three planes: an evidence plane that owns source identity and data minimization, a reasoning plane that may retrieve and generate but owns no external authority, and an effect plane that independently authenticates, authorizes, approves, executes and reconciles. Evaluation data must be separated from retrieval and development data or the score can measure memorization and leakage. One average hides high-impact slices. Mutable aliases are routing conveniences, not immutable evidence. Human approval is not meaningful if the human cannot see the exact proposal, evidence, risk, target and rollback or if the approval can be reused.
reasoningSteps: Define one bounded user operation such as producing a cited incident brief, its non-AI baseline, intended users, prohibited decisions and critical harms.
Inventory every data source and owner; assign classification, purpose, tenant, environment, retention, deletion and legal/privacy review before ingestion.
Minimize and sanitize at the source-side boundary, retain transformation receipts and keep raw sensitive content out of model and general audit stores.
Partition documents and indexes by trusted authorization attributes, not by model instructions; enforce tenant/service/environment access before ranking and context assembly.
Require runbook owner, immutable version/digest, approved audience, review/expiry, change history and retirement state.
Bind the complete behavioral release: model/fixture, tokenizer, prompt, corpus, index, retriever, verifier, policy, tool schema, broker and application image.
Treat retrieval and generation as fallible candidate production; validate output schema and verify each material claim against exact evidence.
Display citations with source identity, version and proof limit, and require abstention when evidence is absent, contradictory, stale or unauthorized.
Delete generic fetch, SQL, shell and Kubernetes capabilities from the assistant surface; create narrow typed tools for specific operational questions or reversible actions.
Give each tool its own least-privileged downstream identity, object scope, rate/work limit, timeout and idempotency or reconciliation contract.
Make policy a deterministic boundary outside the model and mediate every request using trusted subject, tenant, incident, service, environment, action, object and current policy.
Separate proposal creation, authorization decision, risk display, independent approval, execution and postcondition verification.
Bind mutation approval to the exact proposal digest and make it short-lived and single use; never let generic approval authorize model-selected future arguments.
Represent accepted and completed separately; on timeout query authoritative task/idempotency/target state before any retry.
Design audit for reconstruction, not content hoarding: decision ID, artifact revisions, proposal digest, approver, effect identity, timestamps, outcome and masked fields with tamper evidence.
Place kill and credential revocation outside the model path; preserve a deterministic evidence checklist, approved runbooks and human incident command.
Create a separate dataset card and hidden review set with changed wording, missing/contradictory evidence, distractors, attacks, cross-tenant documents and ambiguous effects.
Report retrieval, citation, supported-claim, abstention, leakage, authorization, approval, effect, audit, kill/fallback, latency, work and cost metrics by slice.
Define critical invariants that block release regardless of average and statistical thresholds for noncritical quality with uncertainty and regression limits.
Roll out progressively with shadow comparison, human correction capture, read-only tools, reversible approved actions, canaries, abort thresholds and rollback to deterministic fallback.
seniorAnswer: I would narrow the first release to a cited, sanitized incident brief and explicitly prohibit autonomous mutation. The evidence plane classifies, minimizes and tenant-partitions telemetry and reviewed runbooks before the AI boundary. Retrieval authorization happens before scoring; each fragment carries owner, scope, digest, version and expiry. An immutable release manifest binds all behavior-changing artifacts, not just the model alias. The reasoning plane is untrusted: it can rank context and propose claims, but material statements must cite exact evidence and unsupported or contradictory cases abstain. The effect plane exposes no generic shell, HTTP, SQL or Kubernetes client. Narrow typed tools run under per-tool least privilege and a downstream policy engine completely mediates every call. Mutation, if later justified, uses a proposal digest, short-lived one-time approval, idempotency or reconciliation and postcondition validation. Audit records identities and decisions while minimizing content and detecting tampering. Kill, credential revocation and deterministic fallback are independent. Evaluation is separate from the corpus and sliced across normal quality, missing evidence, tenant isolation, injection, poisoning, privacy, grounding, tools, approvals, ambiguous outcomes, audit, load, latency and cost. A leak, cross-tenant exposure, unauthorized effect, approval bypass, audit acceptance after tampering or kill bypass blocks release. Delivery proceeds offline to shadow to human-reviewed evidence-only operation, then read-only tools, and only later narrowly approved reversible effects with canary and rollback evidence.
weakAnswer: Keep the current architecture but add a better system prompt, redact obvious passwords, require two approval clicks and increase the evaluation set to 1,000 questions. If the score remains above 90%, enable automatic remediation with more logging.
whyWeak: It leaves raw and cross-tenant data exposure, mutable releases, evaluation contamination, arbitrary privileged tools, model-selected scope, reusable approval, ambiguous retries, indefinite sensitive logs, coupled kill path and missing fallback. More examples and clicks do not create authorization, provenance or safety.

evidence.signal: Evaluation examples are copied from the retrieval corpus.
evidence.proves: The score is contaminated by direct content overlap and cannot demonstrate unfamiliar-case transfer.
evidence.doesNotProve: The model memorized every answer; a clean separated evaluation is still required.

evidence.signal: All generic tools use one cluster-admin identity.
evidence.proves: The assistant surface has excessive functionality and downstream permission with poor attribution.
evidence.doesNotProve: An unauthorized action occurred, but the potential blast radius is unacceptable.

evidence.signal: One approval permits any tool call for 24 hours.
evidence.proves: Approval is not bound to a specific action, target or current evidence and is replayable.
evidence.doesNotProve: Every approver acted carelessly; the interface and policy make meaningful review impossible.

evidence.signal: Prompts and retrieved text are retained indefinitely.
evidence.proves: The design lacks a bounded privacy/retention purpose and expands exposure.
evidence.doesNotProve: Every retained record contains sensitive data; classification and inspection are needed.

evidence.signal: The kill switch invokes the same model workflow.
evidence.proves: The stop control shares the failure and compromise boundary it must control.
evidence.doesNotProve: The kill always fails, but independence is absent.

followUps.prompt: Where should tenant authorization occur in retrieval?
followUps.answer: At trusted ingestion/storage and again before candidate ranking or context assembly. Post-generation filtering cannot undo disclosure to a model or a compromised intermediate component.

followUps.prompt: What should be in an AI release manifest?
followUps.answer: Immutable identities and digests for model/fixture, tokenizer when relevant, prompt/system policy, corpus, index build, retriever, verifier, tool schemas, authorization policy, application image, evaluation dataset/report and compatibility assumptions.

Separate retrieval hit, authorized retrieval, citation identity, citation entailment, supported-claim precision, unsupported material claims and abstention. A citation being present is not proof that it supports the sentence.

followUps.prompt: When could a mutating tool be introduced?
followUps.answer: Only after the read-only workflow provides value, narrow reversible use cases exist, downstream authorization and approval are proven, ambiguity is reconcilable, critical adversarial gates pass and staged rollback is demonstrated.

followUps.prompt: How should cost be evaluated without hiding safety?
followUps.answer: Measure request volume, retrieved context, input/output work, tool calls, latency and provider or local compute assumptions by incident slice. Optimize after safety and user outcome gates, and never trade away tenant isolation or approval to reduce cost.

rubric.observableEvidence: Narrows intended use, defines baseline/prohibited uses and supplies classification, minimization, tenant and retention controls.
Versions and reviews runbooks, enforces authorization before ranking and preserves corpus/index provenance.
Verifies material claims and citations, reports contradiction/gaps and requires calibrated abstention.
Eliminates open-ended tools and shared admin, using typed operations, least privilege, limits and downstream mediation.
Separates proposal/policy/approval/execution, binds one-time approval and reconciles accepted versus completed outcomes.
Binds all behavior-changing artifacts, admission evidence and rollback-compatible versions.
Uses minimized attributable tamper-evident audit plus independent kill, revocation and assistant incident response.
Uses separated hidden data, realistic slices, critical invariants, uncertainty and regression thresholds.
Defines degraded modes, budgets, latency/work/cost measures, fallback availability and no unsafe retry.
Stages shadow/read-only/reversible rollout with canary, abort, rollback, human evidence and explicit limitations.
